cands.bio: Taught British literature in public schools for 23 years, including in Rialto. Elected to the Riverside Community College board in 1990. U.S. Representative since 2013 for California's 41st District, now the 39th. Ranking Member of House Veterans' Affairs and a former chair of that committee.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Takano on data centers, local development or growth limits, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. His own site's issue pages that we could read were limited to his biography. He did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so there is no questionnaire on his positions. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we read.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

pro-life.evidence: As of 2022, his abortion-related voting record earned a 100% rating from NARAL Pro-Choice America and an F from the Susan B. Anthony List.

second-amendment.evidence: Supports gun control efforts. After the 2015 San Bernardino attack he criticized Congress for failing to pass gun control laws, calling the shooting "the cost of inaction."

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act, which required DHS to detain certain people in the U.S. without legal permission who were arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting. The bill passed the House 263-156 and was signed into law on 1/29/2025.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 39th Congressional District in 2026. Business owner since 1996 and past president of the Inland Valleys Association of Realtors. Elected to city council in 2012 and served as mayor in 2015, 2019, 2024 and 2026, per his campaign site. Ran for State Assembly District 67 in 2020.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Republican Party of California, per Ballotpedia's 2026 endorsement list.

cands.gaps: His birthplace and where he lived before 1987 are not stated in the pages we could read. His campaign site does not name the city where he serves as council member and mayor. We found no documented stances from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020 or 2026. We found no news coverage or controversies about him.
